Jay mentions Tidal’s numbers scandal to then point out the “Billboard hits” culture of Hip-Hop today. Industry artists often boast about their album sales and Billboard hits, including a young Jay. Even without these sales, Jay debuted the album at number one for the 13th time in a row. line: Three-fifths of a man, I believe’s the phrase
vault_lines: Three-fifths of a man, I believe's the phrase
meaning:
This is a reference to the 3/5th’s compromise of the US Constitution, proposed by James Wilson and Roger Sherman at the Constitutional Convention in 1787. While counting American censuses prior to the end of slavery, each slave was counted as 3/5 of a person. In other words, for every five slaves, three people were counted in the population.

This satisfied the larger, southern states, who could use large slave population to boost national representation, while not having to pay as much in taxes (issues proportionally to the population). At the same time, it somewhat appeased opponents of slavery in the Northern states, who believed that slaves should not be counted.

This compromise, which had major benefits for state power, was at the expense of African-Americans. It dehumanized African-Americans (remember, most blacks in the United States were slaves) and set the tone for their legal disenfranchisement for nearly 2 centuries.

This continues JAY-Z’s statement of irony in the previous line: America may be the land of the free, but since its inception, African-Americans have been treated differently based on the color of their skin.

“Four quarters” is “change,” but it’s also a reference to the way in which Meek has created his own persona and situation through the money he has made himself. It is indicative of how he views his career right now, and a nod to the plethora of “quarter” shout-outs in his music.

We can think that The Game is insinuating that this is because they are black, referencing the constant discrimination African-Americans have been the victim of for decades in the U.S.

PnB Rock (Rakim Hasheem Allen) died after being shot multiple times during a robbery at Roscoe’s Chicken & Waffles in Los Angeles on September 12, 2022. He was dining with his girlfriend when a gunman demanded his jewelry and then shot him before fleeing the scene.

meaning:
In this lyric, Meek is most likely describing a situation that many people go through in prisons across the country, hence the “bunk bed” analogy. If you ever end up in prison, arguably one of the last people you want to have beef with is your cellmate(s). Nighttime lockdowns in most prisons last anywhere from 10 P.M. to 6 A.M., meaning you’re locked in that cell for the next eight or so hours; if the people you’re sharing a cell with have problems with you, that can easily spell disaster.

Through this, Meek outlines a terrifying situation where he could barely get any sleep at night due to fear of being harmed or killed by his own cellmate. That, mixed with the every day drama that can occur in a cellblock, can create a scary situation for both the person incarcerated and their loved ones.

The selling of homemade soul food or “dinner platters” is a common “hustle” around holidays in inner city Philadelphia, and similar urban locations. Since many matriarchs will already be making large meals to feed their family and holiday guests, many make extra food to sell to friends and neighbors.

Dinner platters usually consist of a fried protein, such as chicken or fish, collard greens and baked macaroni and cheese.

This line relates to the last bar where Meek mentions Easter Weekend, a time when many people would be making and selling soul food dinner platters.

ladder is common slang term for an extended ammunition magazine or “clip.”



In this instance, Meek is using the word to refer to the gun in general and/or the ammunition contained in the clip. Since an extended clip holds more bullets than a standard clip, the holder(s) are able to get off more shots at once without the need to reload and are more likely to be able to deliver a shot that will kill the target.

Meek is saying that at the time the boy was being shot to death, the boy’s mother was in the kitchen making food to sell on Easter Weekend.

meaning:
Cutting a deck refers to the procedure where the dealer completes the shuffle, and then sets the cards face-down on the table near the designated player, typically the player to the dealer’s right. The player cuts the deck by removing a contiguous range of cards from the deck, and places them toward himself so that the stack of cards to be dealt is closest to the dealer.

In this case, Meek’s the dealer, and he’s not dealing cards.. he’s dealing coke. Cutting a brick of cocaine refers to diluting the drug to increase its weight and maximize profit.

Also, note the wordplay on shuffle and cut it, since Meek is clearly not in the dope game anymore. He’s “cutting” songs, and a popular option for any playback device is the “shuffle” option. Playing off of the long running trope of comparing making music to making dope, like Kanye previously said in his song “Crack Music”.

line: OG is one who standin’ on his own feet
vault_lines: OG is one who standin' on his own feet
meaning:
The term O.G. is the acronym for Original Gangster with the roots dating back to 1972 when Original was used by the Crips. It was used to insinuate that “we’re first”, the Originals. Two years later the word “Gangster” was added to form the Original Gangster Crips and they only used the term “O.G.” when writing their name or their neighbourhood.

Since then, the term O.G. has been widely used in hip-hop and hood culture in reference to original individuals within a certain area or just someone successful or highly skilled in any given area.

Rick Ross shares more of his wisdom with us in his verse on Ima Boss where he mentions how an O.G. is someone who can take care of themselves, who can achieve success in a certain field. Whereas a boss (pronounced “bawse” by Rick Ross) is someone who guarantees all their boys eat.

To expand this further, the term eat is used to describe success in such a way that everyone reaps and benefits from it. The prime example of this as always is a figure such as Jay-Z, who throughout the years has guaranteed quite a few people gon’ eat.

To quote him on this from his verse on “Pound Cake”:

I’ve done made more millionaires than the lotto did
Dame made millions, Biggs made millions
Ye made millions, Just made millions
Lyor made millions, Cam made millions
Beans’a tell you if he wasn’t in his feelings
